title: Generating set-cogenerated cotorsion pairs: smallness and filtrations
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] in a fixed universe, $S$ a set of objects, $\mathcal T=S^{\perp_1}$, and $\mathcal L={}^{\perp_1}\mathcal T$. Here $\operatorname{Ext}^1(U,V)=0$ means that every short exact sequence $0\to V\to E\to U\to0$ splits; the orthogonals require this against every object of the given class. Suppose $G\in\mathcal L$ is a generator, meaning every object is an epimorphic image of a small coproduct of copies of $G$.
Then $(\mathcal L,\mathcal T)$ is a complete cotorsion pair: $\mathcal T=\mathcal L^{\perp_1}$, and every object $X$ occurs in short exact sequences $0\to T\to L\to X\to0$ and $0\to X\to T'\to L'\to0$ with $L,L'\in\mathcal L$ and $T,T'\in\mathcal T$. There is a set $I$ of monomorphisms, each with cokernel isomorphic to an object of $S\cup\{G\}$, whose right lifting class is exactly the epimorphisms with kernel in $\mathcal T$. Right lifting means every commutative square with a left map in $I$ admits a diagonal filler. Moreover $\mathcal L$ consists exactly of retracts of $S\cup\{G\}$-filtered objects. An $S\cup\{G\}$-filtered object is the colimit of a small ordinal-indexed continuous increasing chain of subobjects starting at zero, with each successor quotient isomorphic to an object of $S\cup\{G\}$; continuity means that at a limit ordinal the subobject is the colimit of the preceding subobjects. A retract has maps $X\to Y\to X$ with composite $1_X$. No enough-projectives hypothesis is required.
